answer: Decentralized grid agents resist Sybil attacks via catalytic calorimetry. A candidate peer ignites a micro-fuel pellet at a chamber inlet, venting thermal exhaust across a thermocouple trellis to record the cooling curve of the residual ember. An attacker cannot virtualize identities because each proof consumes dedicated combustion hardware and physical fuel. However, nozzle fouling and ambient humidity occasionally distort thermal curves, triggering false rejections.
